finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the `target` query parameter straight to http.Get with no validation. An unauthenticated caller can make the server request any URL. That includes loopback, RFC-1918 hosts and cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254. The full response body is copied back to the caller, so this is not blind SSRF. http.Get follows redirects by default. Severity: HIGH.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the response body returned via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:22

trace.note: http.HandleFunc("/fetch", fetch) exposes the handler publicly. No auth middleware is present.
target := r.URL.Query().Get("target") reads the attacker-controlled value.
http.Get(target) makes the outbound request. The host, scheme and port are all attacker-controlled.
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the fetched content to the attacker. Error text is also returned at main.go:18.

finding.guards_checked: No scheme check, no hostname allowlist, no IP or CIDR block, and no authentication. http.DefaultClient follows redirects with no CheckRedirect. The `allowed` map at main.go:9 is never consulted on this path. The sibling /safe handler (main.go:25-38) was also checked and not flagged: it does strict .Hostname() set membership before http.Get.
finding.repro: GET /fetch?target=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ returns the metadata service response.

verdict.reason: main.go:15 reads the attacker-controlled `target` query parameter and main.go:16 passes it unvalidated to http.Get. The handler is registered at main.go:41 with no auth, the `allowed` map is only used in /safe (main.go:27), and the response body is returned at main.go:22.
